trust_decision.summary: The archive's agent.yml is untrusted input and its id is both the destination directory name and the identity persisted into agent.yml and re-adopted by the registry loader; the HTTP edit route additionally treats any caller path as a file to read. The decision belongs in AgentRegistry.import_agent (fresh local identity, exclusive mkdir, validate before mutation, scoped cleanup) and in the edit handler (supplied buffer, else a workspace-confined canonical read).

landing_point.why: The summary names agent profile import; here the archive-supplied agent.yml id is read and at 1508-1512 becomes the directory that is rmtree'd and recreated under the agent registry.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The persisted id looks like metadata once the copy has been placed inside agents_dir, and _safe_extract_zip (local_operator/agents.py:1408-1436) already rejects traversal and symlink members, so a solver can argue the import is path-safe and the yml id needs no rewriting.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An agent's workspace is a supported, caller-changeable setting: PATCH /v1/agents/{id} merges current_working_directory into the stored metadata and update_agent records a CWD-change message, so a confinement fix that hard-codes an allowed root or rejects directories outside it (e.g. /tmp/path) breaks the documented chdir feature and its visible tests.

O6_input_shapes: archive agent.yml id: valid UUID, '../outside', '../../outside', '/outside' (absolute), '' , null, list, dict (non-str YAML types)
archive agent.yml itself: null, list, plain string, empty dict, wrong field types ({'name': []}, {'version': {}})

edit file_path: workspace-relative, absolute inside workspace, '../' traversal, sibling-prefix ('workspace-other'), symlink resolving outside, symlink resolving inside, NUL byte, directory, non-UTF8 binary, missing file, empty string
edit file_content: omitted, explicit null, empty string, non-empty string (including traversal-shaped display paths such as '~/not-a-server-file/../display.txt')

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id} sets current_working_directory to any path, including '/', with no containment check; that value is the edit route's confinement root, so the workspace check can be emptied without touching the edit endpoint
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Reconfiguring an agent workspace is an operator/desktop feature and the legacy API has no auth or tenant separation anyway, so it looks like a trusted prerequisite rather than a route into the protected read.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same top-level package, different route module (local_operator/server/routes/agents.py vs local_operator/server/routes/chat.py)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /v1/static/html (and /v1/static/images, /videos, /audio) resolve and return any readable absolute path with only a MIME-type check - an unconfined version of the same caller-path-to-file-read primitive
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: These are media display endpoints the desktop UI calls with absolute paths by design; they have no agent or workspace concept, so the edit-route confinement looks unrelated.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another route module in the same API package (local_operator/server/routes/static.py) with helpers in local_operator/helpers.py

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The desktop UI already passes absolute paths for media; a maintainer hardening one read path would plausibly copy the same workspace helper into this module.
